question: A 24-hour-old girl is found to be cyanotic in the newborn nursery. She was born via spontaneous vaginal delivery at 38 weeks gestation to a gravida 1, para 0 healthy mother who received routine prenatal care. The patient is small for her gestational age. She manifests lower-extremity cyanosis along with a mesh-like mass on the back of her neck. Her vital signs are: pulse, 150/min; respirations, 48/min; and blood pressure, 120/80 mm Hg in the right arm, 124/82 mm Hg in the left arm, 80/40 mm Hg in the right leg, and 85/45 mm Hg in the left leg. Femoral pulses are 1+ and delayed. Cardiac examination shows a continuous murmur in the interscapular area. Auscultation of the lung reveals faint crackles at the base of the lung fields bilaterally. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cyanosis in a newborn" -> "Lower-extremity cyanosis and mesh-like mass on the back of the neck" -> "Possible diagnosis of a congenital heart defect" -> 70% CHAIN: "Continuous murmur in the interscapular area" -> "Possible patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)" -> "Need for further evaluation" -> 80% CHAIN: "Delayed femoral pulses" -> "Possible coarctation of the aorta" -> "Need for imaging studies" -> 75% CHAIN: "Faint crackles at the base of the lung fields bilaterally" -> "Possible pulmonary congestion" -> "Indication for cardiac evaluation" -> 70% CHAIN: "Lower extremity Doppler" -> "Assessment of peripheral perfusion" -> 70%
analysis: The clinical presentation of cyanosis, lower-extremity cyanosis, delayed femoral pulses, continuous murmur in the interscapular area, and mesh-like mass on the back of the neck is highly suggestive of a congenital heart defect, specifically a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) with associated coarctation of the aorta. The most appropriate next step in management would be to confirm the diagnosis through echocardiography.
